q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a kitchen chimney?
title: Kitchen chimney carbon footprint per unit
short: Add the steel or glass hood, motor and blower, filters and controls per chimney with supplier figures. Add sheet metal work, painting, assembly and testing energy, then divide by chimneys built.

ul: Stainless or painted steel hood, or glass panel.
Baffle or filter set and lights.
Cutting, bending and welding of the hood.

p: Report per chimney by width and suction rating.

example.title: Worked example: kitchen chimney unit per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 7,100 / 3,000 = 2.367 kg CO2 per unit
Add hood steel, motor and filters for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
